fieldValues.title: A struct field set to None everywhere is a signal, not noise
fieldValues.summary: Grepping every construction site of a field across the codebase and finding it is always None (or always the same literal) in fixtures and tests is a fast, general way to find a field the type model carries but no code path actually consumes.
fieldValues.rationale: Confirming srs-rust#958's editorHint claim didn't require reading every consumer by hand: grepping `EditorHint|editor_hint` across crates/*/src showed every non-definition site assigning `editor_hint: None` in a fixture, with zero reads anywhere outside the round-tripping field_json.rs shim. That pattern generalizes past this one field — before assuming a schema-correct property is honored downstream, grep its construction sites; if they are uniformly a placeholder value in test/fixture code and never a live read, the property is declared but unwired, and the fix is to wire it, not to add another test asserting the placeholder.
